balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Albemarle Corporation: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Albemarle Corporation: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

segmentRevenue.title: Segment revenue
segmentRevenue.content:
Albemarle reports three operating segments: Energy Storage (lithium for EV and grid batteries), Specialties (bromine, lithium specialties and other fine chemicals) and Ketjen (refining catalysts).

For Albemarle Corporation: Energy Storage is ~70% of consolidated revenue, so its lithium-price cycle dominates the top line; Ketjen was divested in March 2026 and 2026 filings instead report a residual "Corporate and all other" line, which is why Ketjen bars stop and a new series starts.

What to watch:

  • Energy Storage revenue relative to spot lithium carbonate/hydroxide prices, not just volumes shipped
  • Specialties (bromine) as the more stable, less commoditized segment
  • The Ketjen-to-Corporate transition break in 2026

segmentEbitda.title: Segment Adjusted EBITDA
segmentEbitda.content:
Management's non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA by segment, excluding restructuring, impairments and other significant items.

For Albemarle Corporation: Energy Storage Adjusted EBITDA fell from a peak above $3.3bn in FY2022 to under $700m by FY2024-25 as spot lithium prices collapsed 85-95% from their January 2023 peak, even though Specialties and Ketjen EBITDA stayed comparatively stable -- the segment split shows the earnings collapse was almost entirely a lithium-price event, not an operating failure.

What to watch:

  • Energy Storage EBITDA margin troughing and recovering with the lithium price cycle
  • Specialties (bromine) EBITDA as the earnings floor when lithium is weak

energyStoragePriceVolume.title: Energy Storage: price vs. volume impact
energyStoragePriceVolume.content:
Albemarle discloses the year-over-year change in Energy Storage net sales as a decomposition into a price impact (change in realized lithium pricing, including contract mechanisms) and a volume impact (change in tonnes sold), each in dollars.

For Albemarle Corporation: from FY2023 to FY2025 the price impact was deeply negative each year (e.g. -$5.4bn in FY2024) while volume impact stayed positive or roughly flat -- confirming the earnings decline was a pricing collapse, not a demand or share-loss problem; price impact turned positive again in 2026 as lithium prices recovered.

What to watch:

  • Price impact flipping from negative to positive as the signal the cycle has turned
  • Whether volume impact stays positive through the downturn (demand intact) or turns negative (demand destruction)

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Albemarle Corporation: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Albemarle Corporation: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Albemarle Corporation: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Albemarle Corporation: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Albemarle Corporation: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Albemarle Corporation: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Albemarle Corporation: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Albemarle Corporation: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
